AQ5NpMY7p8AViNlD.name: Quick start
AQ5NpMY7p8AViNlD.content:
The module adds a skyship sheet with a builder, turns a ship into a real Foundry scene made of tiles, regions and walls, and builds a battle scene for two ships.

  1. Create an actor of type “Skyship” (or open the example ship in the “SkyPlane” folder).
  2. On the Builder tab drag compartments from the catalog, the “SkyPlane: compartments” compendium or the Items tab onto the grid.
  3. On the Crew tab drag character actors into the list. Assign characters to players (User Configuration): the module uses them to tell which side a player is on.
  4. On the Parameters tab press “Deploy to scene”. Place tokens on the scene the usual way.
  5. In the module settings open “Crew permissions” and give players their checkboxes.

Set the ship image on the Parameters tab — it shows in the actor list, on the token and on the scene's parameter plate. A battle of two ships starts with “Start battle…” on the ship sheet; see “Combat and scouting”. Your own compartment catalogs are described in “Builder and passage rules”.

iGFudfA5eZkb0Vxb.name: Builder and passage rules
iGFudfA5eZkb0Vxb.content:
The ship grid is up to 14×8 squares, 11×6 by default. Compartment sizes in the book are written as “height×length”; compartments do not rotate.

  • A ship needs at least one “Control” and one “Engine room” compartment — otherwise it is an error. Errors do not block deployment.
  • A compartment cannot be placed outside the map, on top of another one, or so that an “Outside only” compartment ends up enclosed on all sides.
  • Warnings: a compartment does not touch others; compartments are not connected by passages; the crew does not fit.

Passages

  • Horizontal — between side neighbours whose bottom rows are level. The opening is only as high as the bottom square.
  • Vertical — a ladder above or below a ladder, the opening along the shared border.
  • From the GM — the “Passage up” / “Passage down” checkboxes in the compartment window open a passage along the whole shared border; one checkbox on either side is enough.

“Ignores passage” compartments are left out of the connectivity check.

Compartment catalog

Hover a catalog compartment in the builder: matching compartments on the grid light up, the rest dim.

The GM creates custom compartments with “New” — they appear in the “SkyPlane” item folder. The pencil on a world compartment opens its sheet; the pencil on a compendium compartment creates a copy in the world with the same identifier, and the copy replaces the original in the catalog. The bin removes a world compartment from the catalog. Compartments already placed on ships are independent copies: to carry a catalog edit over to them, the GM presses “Update on ships” on the compartment sheet. Position, passages and damage taken are kept; if the new size does not fit, the old one stays.

Compartment catalogs

The list above the builder palette picks the catalog: “SkyPlane: compartments”, “SkyPlane: StarCraft II compartments” or your own. Each client remembers its choice.

Your own catalog is an Item compendium in the “SkyPlane Combat Re:verse” folder. The GM creates one with the folder button next to the list: gives it a name and, if wanted, copies the compartments of the current catalog (the copies get new identifiers and are not linked to the originals). An Item compendium created by hand on the Compendiums tab and moved into this folder becomes a catalog too.

Your own catalog is not locked: “New” creates a compartment right in it, the pencil opens the compartment sheet with all fields, active effects and combat properties, the bin deletes the compartment from the catalog. Compartments already placed stay on the ships; “Update on ships” carries an edit over. Players with the “Build the ship” permission see the catalog if they can access the compendium (observer by default). A catalog is deleted like any compendium: right-click it on the Compendiums tab.

Undo. Ctrl+Z in an open builder undoes the last placement, move or removal of a compartment, a map resize or the starter kit — up to 50 steps per ship. Damage and repairs made between the steps are not rolled back. The key can be changed in Foundry's controls settings.

Export and import. In the ship sheet header menu (GM): “Export to JSON” saves the ship to a file, “Import from JSON” replaces this ship with it — compartments, stats, crew. Scene, log and permissions stay; crew actors missing from the world are dropped. Rebuild the scene after an import.

Stats

Hull = ⌈compartments without “No hull points” ÷ 3⌉ × 100; crew capacity = intact “Residential” compartments; speed is the maximum and fuel economy the minimum among intact engine rooms. Active effects of compartments change these values while the compartment is intact, and every breach costs 1 speed. A manual edit on the sheet holds until the next change of the layout or the “Recalculate by the rules” button.

dwSfW3vqoEolP8cv.name: Ship scene
dwSfW3vqoEolP8cv.content:
“Deploy to scene” creates an ordinary scene in side view: the parameter area on the left, the ship map on the right, the description and system tables below.

  • The Foundry grid is 100 px, 5 ft; one ship square is 2×2 cells, 200 px, 10 ft, and holds 4 medium tokens.
  • Every compartment gets a locked tile and a region. Walls block movement only; openings follow the passage rules.
  • Narrow, damaged and breached compartments are difficult terrain (the “Modify Movement Cost” region behaviour).
  • The compartment plate shows HP, conditions (“Burning”, “Breach”, “Smoke”) and the gun's ammo; the parameter plate shows the ship image (hidden for an unrevealed enemy).
  • Labels, frames and areas are drawn on each client and are not stored as documents. Clicking the ship name opens the sheet, clicking a compartment plate opens the compartment window.

HP changes update the scene by themselves. When a compartment is added, moved or removed, the sheet shows a “scene is out of date” mark — press “Rebuild”. A rebuild replaces only the generated objects; tokens and the GM's own objects stay.

z1u5QC2mdNSBFeWi.name: Combat and scouting
z1u5QC2mdNSBFeWi.content:
On the ship sheet the GM presses “Start battle…” and picks the enemy: the ship the button was pressed on goes on the left. Tokens from the ship scenes are copied to the same places on the map. The GM activates the battle scene for the players.

The distance is shared by the pair: a change in battle is written to both sheets. Each ship has its own phlogiston.

Moving a token to the other ship. In Foundry v13 walls stop dragging even for the GM. Turn on the “Unconstrained Movement” tool in the token controls, move the token and turn the tool off.

Round and distance

A round is an ordinary dnd5e combat: the combat tracker, initiative, turns. The battle phase starts at medium distance; after that the GM changes it by hand to fit the story.

DistanceEffect
MediumNo penalties
ClosePenalty for guns without “Close” checked (long-range guns)
FarPenalty for guns without “Far” checked (close-range guns); evasive manoeuvres are more effective
MeleeDisadvantage on hits for all guns; turbulence

The penalty is added to the hit DC; its size is set in the module settings (“Gun range penalty”, 5 by default). Each gun has checkboxes for the distances without a penalty — for example “Medium and Far” for the “Carbolin”. Active effects of the ships change the DC too: the shooter's accuracy lowers it, the target's defense raises it (see “Active effects”).

Firing

  1. A character stands in an intact compartment with firepower on their own ship: they came there on their turn or stood there at the start of it.
  2. They open the compartment window (click the plate), press “Fire” and pick a compartment of the enemy ship on the canvas. Right click or Esc cancels.
  3. A check of the gun's skill is rolled against its DC for the current distance.
  4. On a success the dnd5e damage window opens: normal or critical damage and a situational bonus.
  5. The damage goes both to the ship's hull and to the HP of the chosen compartment.

After a hit a card appears in the chat. By default the damage applies at once, and the GM's card has an “Undo” button — it restores exactly what the hit took from the hull and the compartment. If the “GM applies damage” checkbox is on in the module settings, the damage waits for “Apply” or “Reject”. A damage number floats above the compartment, and a tracer flies from the gun to the target: an orange flash for a hit, a grey puff beside the target for a miss. Animations are turned off in the client settings (“Interface animations”).

The GM battle panel lists each ship's guns: “ready”, “fired”, “destroyed”, “empty”, and for charging guns “not charged”, “charging” and “charged”. The fire button next to a ready gun fires for the crew: the token in the gun shoots if there is one, otherwise the captain or the first crew member; with no crew it is a plain d20 against the gun's DC.

Each gun fires once per round (if the tracker combat has started). You can fire at an unrevealed ship — blindly. The “Fight” checkbox in the permission matrix is required.

A gun is set up on the compartment sheet: hit skill and DC, distances without a penalty (“Close”, “Medium”, “Far” checkboxes), ammo, special property and damage (number of dice, d4–d20 die, bonus).

Special guns

  • Splash (flamethrower). Compartments sharing a side with the target take half the damage (rounded down) — only to their own HP, the ship's hull is untouched. The hit also sets the target on fire. “Undo” on the card restores the splash too.
  • Charge (Yamato cannon). The first press of “Charge” uses the gun's shot this round; it can fire from the next round. Firing removes the charge. Without a started tracker combat the shot is available right after charging.
  • Volley (ATA lasers, interceptors). Each damage die is a separate shot: its own target, its own hit check and one damage die (plus the bonus). Right click or Esc while picking a target ends the volley early — the shots already made count.

Ammo

The compartment sheet of a gun has an “Ammo (shots)” field: 0 means unlimited. Each shot (and a whole volley) uses one charge; an empty gun does not fire and shows “empty” on the battle panel. The GM reloads in the compartment window: a number of charges or the “Reload” button. In the compendiums the “Bumblebee” torpedoes (4) and the Yamato cannon (3) are limited.

Compartment conditions

ConditionSourceEffectRemoved by
BurningA flamethrower hitAt the start of every combat round the compartment takes 1d6 damage to its own HP; checks in it have disadvantage“Extinguish” in the compartment window: a crew member in the compartment, Athletics, DC 12, with disadvantage; a destroyed compartment goes out by itself
BreachA critical hitDifficult terrain, −1 to the ship's speedRepairing the compartment with a consumable
SmokeThe GMChecks in the compartment (firing, scouting, extinguishing) have disadvantageClears at the start of the next round

The GM sets and removes any condition with the checkboxes in the compartment window. “Undo” on a hit card also removes the conditions that hit applied. Rounds are counted by the combat tracker on the battle scene; stepping a round back does not burn again.

End of battle

The GM battle panel has an “End battle” button: pick the players' ship (the module guesses it from the crew) and the outcome — victory or defeat. The tracker combat on this scene is deleted, the fired and charged marks are cleared, and the result goes to the chat and to the logs of both ships. The players' ship scene is activated — everyone moves to it, and “Victory” or “Defeat” floats above it. The battle scene stays: the next battle of the same pair is rebuilt on it.

Scouting

A crew member in an intact “Recon” compartment of their own ship opens the compartment window and presses “Scout”: a check of the radar's skill is rolled. On a success their side sees the whole enemy ship while the scout stays at the post.

The GM decides over the scouting on the battle panel: “Reveal” shows the enemy, “Hide” hides it even after a successful scouting, “Auto” clears the GM decision and reveal follows scouting again. Until then the enemy is a silhouette: dark rectangles, only the name and class; tokens on it are hidden, except tokens of your own side.

A player's side is the ship whose crew includes one of their actors (the same rule as for matrix permissions). If their actors are on both ships, the assigned character decides. The GM sees everything.

xJ5rO2RiCoGoFvGR.name: Active effects
xJ5rO2RiCoGoFvGR.content:
A catalog compartment can carry Foundry active effects (ActiveEffect). A ship counts the effects of a compartment while it is intact (or works when destroyed), the GM's “Effect active” checkbox in the compartment window is on and the effect itself is not disabled.

Where to set them up

Catalog compartment sheet → “Active effects” block. Pick a preset (one change of +1, +100 for hull) or “Blank effect” and press “Add” — Foundry's standard effect window opens: name, icon, the “Changes” tab. The toggle enables and disables an effect, the bin deletes it.

When placed on a ship, the effects are copied into the compartment. “Update on ships” carries edits of catalog effects over to placed copies. All effects of a ship and the resulting bonuses are shown on the Systems tab of the ship sheet.

Keys

KeyWhat it changes
system.maxHpShip hull
system.maxCrewCrew capacity
system.speedSpeed
system.fuelEconomyFuel economy
system.bonuses.attackGun accuracy: the hit DC of this ship's guns is lower by the value
system.bonuses.damageGun damage: added to the damage formula (for a volley — to each shot)
system.bonuses.defenseDefense: the DC to hit this ship is higher by the value
system.bonuses.repairConsumable repair: each consumable restores more HP
system.bonuses.scoutScouting: the scouting check DC is lower by the value

Modes

“Add” (a negative value subtracts), “Multiply”, “Upgrade”, “Downgrade”, “Override” — in priority order, as in Foundry. The “Custom” mode and other keys are ignored by the module.

Hull, crew capacity, speed and fuel economy are recalculated when the layout changes, a compartment is destroyed or repaired, and “Effect active” is toggled. When a compartment that adds hull is destroyed, the maximum drops and the current hull does not exceed the new maximum; after a repair the maximum comes back, the current hull does not.

Examples in the compendiums

  • “Shield Generator” (protoss): hull +200.
  • “Defensive Matrix” (terran): hull +100.
  • “Marine Barracks”: crew capacity +2.
  • “Repair Workshop”: consumable repair +2.
  • “Lookout Post (“Crow's Nest”)”: scouting +2.

The old “Stat modifier” of compartments turns into the same kind of active effect when the world is updated.

JUj5XmqpDrmBh8BU.name: Repair
JUj5XmqpDrmBh8BU.content:
A player with the “Repair” permission presses “Repair…” in the compartment window and picks a consumable of their character in the crew. One piece is used up, the compartment's HP grows by the consumable's amount (not above the maximum). A destroyed compartment that gets HP back works again, and a breach in the compartment is closed.

A repair consumable is an ordinary dnd5e item with the flags.skyplane-combat-reverse.repair.amount flag. Presets are in the “SkyPlane: repair consumables” compendium. Any item can be marked with a macro:

game.modules.get("skyplane-combat-reverse").api.markRepairItem(item, 10);

hT0DDT8Yv2BaZv6I.name: Permissions
hT0DDT8Yv2BaZv6I.content:
Players are observers of the ship; every change goes to the GM's client through socketlib, and the GM checks the permission before writing. If no GM is online — a notification, nothing changes.

PermissionWhat it opens
Edit parametersName, class, image, captain, numbers on the Parameters tab, description
Build the shipThe builder
RepairThe “Repair…” and “Extinguish” buttons
Phlogiston and distanceThe phlogiston scale and the distance plates
FightFiring and scouting

A permission works only on ships whose crew includes one of the player's actors — the same rule decides the player's side in battle. GM only: scenes, starting a battle, crew, damage, passages, conditions, ammo, reveal, log, permission matrix.

nEl2gcvB9bDvYDOk.name: Ship templates
nEl2gcvB9bDvYDOk.content:
The “SkyPlane: ship templates” compendium holds ready-made skyships. Drag a template into the actor folder, deploy it to a scene and edit it in the builder: the copy is independent of the template.

ShipClassMapWhy it is interesting
SwiftCourier9×3The smallest ship: one deck, two cabins
GrumblerCargo barque12×5Three holds, a captain's cabin, slow and tough
HarpyGunboat10×4Six guns on three decks, a flamethrower and torpedoes
LeviathanHeavy cruiser14×7The largest size, a “Pacific Titan”, 800 HP
HyperionBattlecruiser (StarCraft II)14×5Yamato cannon, defensive matrix (+100 HP), GM “Passage down” hatches
Wrath of AiurProtoss carrier (StarCraft II)14×4Four “Outside only” hangars, a shield generator (+200 HP)

The compartments of the last two are in the “SkyPlane: StarCraft II compartments” compendium. It is a joke, not official content: the rules are the same as for the other compartments.

MWhqgeTAvCgTngL6.name: Macros and API
MWhqgeTAvCgTngL6.content:
API: game.modules.get("skyplane-combat-reverse").api. Methods take an actor or a UUID.

  • deployShip(ship), rebuildScene(scene), startBattle(left, right)
  • damageShip(ship, n), healShip(ship, n), damageCompartment(ship, instanceId, n)
  • repairCompartment(ship, instanceId, {amount | itemUuid})
  • setPhlogiston(ship, 0–5), setDistance(ship, "melee"|"close"|"medium"|"far")
  • setReveal(scene, "left"|"right", true|false), validateShip(ship), markRepairItem(item, n), openBattlePanel()
  • fireWeapon(ship, instanceId) — fire as your own token in the gun, scout(ship, instanceId) — scouting check

Hooks (called on every client): skyplaneCombatReverse.compartmentDestroyed, .compartmentRestored, .compartmentRepaired, .shipDisabled, .revealChanged, .sceneBuilt, .compartmentHit (ship, compartment, damage; negative when undone), .shipFired (ship, gun, target ship, target compartment, damage; for a volley — once per shot).

The “Deploy ship”, “Start battle” and “Battle panel” macros are in the “SkyPlane: macros” compendium.

skyHelpInventory.name: Inventory
skyHelpInventory.content:
Compartments with a grid (by default the Cargo hold 10×6, the Workshop 6×4, cabins 3×3) have an inventory. The grid size is on the Inventory tab of the compartment sheet; 0 means no inventory.

Access

The compartment window has an Inventory button. A player opens it only while their character's token stands in that compartment (on the ship or battle scene, including an enemy ship's compartment when boarding). If the token leaves, the window stays view-only. The GM sees every compartment's inventory.

Items

  • Drag an item from a character sheet onto the grid: a “How many?” slider appears; the item is moved, not copied.
  • Drag an item from the grid onto a character sheet, onto another compartment's grid or another ship's.
  • While an item is dragged on the grid, F rotates it (change it in the keybinding settings).
  • Right-click: Rotate, Size…, Split stack…, Take, Delete (GM).
  • Identical items (same source) share one stack. Default sizes: consumable and loot 1×1, equipment and tool 1×2, weapon 1×3, container 2×2. A container moves together with its contents.

GM catalog

The left side of the inventory window lists the module's cargo and repair kits and your own item compendiums in the “SkyPlane Combat Re:verse” folder, with search and a type filter. “New cargo” creates a Loot item in the “Custom cargo” compendium.

Ammunition

On a gun's sheet, Combat tab, the Ammunition field: drop an item there. A gun with an Ammo capacity is reloaded with the Reload button in the compartment window — rounds are taken from the gun compartment's inventory up to a full magazine. A gun without Ammo capacity but with Ammunition uses one round from its compartment's inventory per shot or volley. The torpedo launcher and the Yamato cannon already use “Bumblebee” torpedoes and Yamato charges from the cargo compendium.

Every store, take, transfer and reload goes to the ship log — filter “Inventory”.
